pages.text: Festival preparations filled the village square. The grown-ups gave them a box of paper-flower garlands.
They wanted to hang the flowers themselves. "Would it look nice all along the wall?"
Riri spread her hand to measure spaces. Lolo climbed onto a box. "Even spaces will look nice." "Hanging them high will look nice."
Riri measured one handspan, then two. Not one flower had been hung.
The wind shook the garland. Riri began measuring all over again.
Standing on the box, Lolo rose onto tiptoe. Lolo's fingertips could barely reach the wall's top.
The box collapsed. Paper flowers tumbled onto Lolo's head.
The flowers looked like a crown. Seeing it, Riri climbed onto Lolo's shoulders.
With Riri on those shoulders, Lolo walked along the wall. Riri hung the garlands one after another.
Garlands hung neatly along the wall. The flower crown was still on Lolo's head. The grown-ups saw it and clapped.
